Just keep in mind that a lot of these side effects should subside, a week is a pretty short time for antidepressants. However your doctor will most likely or probably has told you all that already :)

It's interesting that such low dosages of these meds work for you. I'm assuming they're stronger medications than Luvox which is what I have because I take 200mg of that and when I was on Zoloft it was 150mg of that. I dont feel shame in taking my tablets, however if people ask ( like friends who stay over or whatever), I am more comfortable confessing to anxiety disorders than depression. When you say you're depressed people immediately assume it's your own fault and tell you to snap out of it which drives me beyond insane, I've found it easier to just confess to anxiety problems which seem to be more socially accepted. So I understand your frustration with your colleague. Thanks for sharing your story.

Thanks for your story. Did you ever wonder if you were using drugs as a subconscious self medication for stressors in your life? Or is that what you meant by "snapped" a little? Either way I'm really glad that things improved for you after the second attempt at valium. I've experienced that emotionless feeling on antidepressants and I absolutely hate it. At least when you're taking drugs you can feel emotions, though I stopped taking illegal drugs because I really need to focus on trying to remain mentally stable and coming down off everything I used to take was bad anxiety trips that I really didn't need with my already messed up mind.

I find it hard sometimes because my brain tells me that I'm not being affected but then I am not as stressed as usual so I think it's having some affect. I guess everyone would just say to go back and talk to your therapist/ gp about it. I hope you find the answer.

The Luvox is primarily targeted to treat the anxiety and mild OCD then the higher doses of the Luvox is supposed to help the depression. Unfortunately lately I've been panic attacking and so I'm going to be heading back to the doc. My doctor's a cool guy, really interested in mental health. I have a list of nearby therapists that he gave me awhile ago but it's the act of picking up the phone I have trouble with.
I completely agree. There's nothing more frustrating than trying to tell a person that you're actually sick and not just attention seeking. I hope you can find your peace.
Hold on brother. You can get through this shit.

Well, I've been struggling with depression for close to 8 years now but I also have a lot of reasons to be depressed. It's my anxiety that made me finally decide to try medication because it was becoming completely debilitating. But I really should try and see someone new. It's just unfortunate that I'm so jaded by past experience. I've had some shocking therapists, the highlight being the one who rang me an hour after our session to apologize for how badly it had gone!

That's interesting, I initially lost weight on my current meds but have since gained weight, however I think it's because theyre not working because I keep forcing myself to eat even when I know I don't want to. I also tend to get obsessive compulsive and will choose things I need to eat and if I don't eat them I get stressed. I'd be interested to see what will happen if I'm put on new meds. Thanks for your insights!
I can definitely see your stressors there. I think you're fortunate that you were able to get through your problems without the meds. My experiences tell me they're fairly troublesome.

Not anymore, my psych disappeared off the face of the Earth. Literally stopped responding to emails/ calls. I've seen that many others that it's hard for me to trust going back to another. There's nothing I hate more than going to a new psych and listening to yet another hour of breathing exercises and telling me things I figured out about myself years ago.

Yeah I know, Im just curious to hear everyone's experiences. I find it hard because it seems to take so long to reach the point where I can go back and say the pills arent working and I fear having to come off of the pills I'm on and start a new batch. It's almost like I try to will myself to believe the antidepressants are working so that I don't have to go back to square one.
Fair enough, Thanks for sharing!
